statement: The essential-matrix five-point problem has full symmetric monodromy S10.

group.description: S10 in its natural action on the ten projective essential matrices

notes:
This corollary has a geometric proof. The larger 20- and 40-sheet pose covers have different monodromy.

LMFDB identification: 10T45 in the recorded permutation degree. Standard generating permutations, when newly supplied here, are an abstract relabeling of the proved group action; they are not additional path-tracking data.

Duff et al. explicitly describe Corollary 4.2 as a geometric version of Nistér–Hartley–Stewénius, Section 5. The 2007 paper is the result association; Duff’s geometric proof remains the inspected verification source.

The following bibliography supplies historical attribution or supporting background for the result. David Nistér, Richard Hartley, Henrik Stewénius, Using Galois Theory to Prove Structure from Motion Algorithms are Optimal (2007, nister_hartley_stewenius_2007_galois).
